newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada minutes say recovery well under way.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada minutes say recovery well under way.

text.p: An increasing number of economic indicators suggested Canada's economic recovery was well under way, minutes from the Bank of Canada's May 8 board of directors' meeting released on Wednesday said.
"Recent information suggested a marked acceleration in the pace of economic expansion in Canada since the beginning of the year," the minutes cited Governor Gordon Thiessen as saying.
"Both external and domestic factors pointed to continued economic expansion and a pickup in employment in coming months."
Thiessen also said he expected external demand to resume its role as an important contributor to the Canadian economy this year, helped by the strong competitive position of Canadian industry.
The board said they also expected consumer spending to be strong, led by interest-sensitive sectors.
"In Canada, accommodative monetary conditions are having the anticipated stimulative effect on aggregate demand," the minutes said.
The Bank of Canada has continuously loosened monetary conditions over the past year in an attempt to stimulate Canada's sluggish economy.
But the Bank of Canada board said rising inflation should not be an immediate concern because of the current state of excess supply in the Canadian economy.

The bank noted that one sign of a strengthening Canadian economy was the growth of M1, a narrow measure of the amount of money in circulation. M1 increased "at the unsustainable rate of 15.5 percent in March" year over year, the minutes said.
The report said part of the strength of M1 was stimulated by low interest rates and changes in banking practices.
"Nevertheless, persistent M1 growth at such rates is not consistent with preserving low inflation," the minutes said.
The minutes noted that prospects amoung Canada's major trading partners were for expanding economic activity and continuing low inflation.
The board said the average price of key primary commodities exported by Canada continued to be favorable.
